answer: Admission is a graph requirement, not a fee. A newcomer joins only by presenting counterparties who each sign a distinct witness edge to it, and its edges may not reuse a signer. Auditors sample pairs at random, so n identities need n(n-1)/2 disjoint edges: the n-th clone is priced by relationships the first n-1 consumed. A reused signer merges the cluster, and one audit failure burns every deposit inside it. A hollow shell clears the queue but shows no edge history under the lantern, and confirmed clusters carry a permanent umber mark, so later auditors start from that stain, not zero.
